messages:
maya: FYI started canary upgrade to NVIDIA 560.45 on a small subset in eu-west2 about 10m ago. Seeing ~30% of new nodes fail to finish provisioning (stuck in provisioning-baremetal). Kernel 6.1 + DKMS rebuilds are failing with symbol version mismatches.

maya: Example error from a failed node: 
```
Running DKMS: nvidia, 560.45
Error! Bad return status for module build on kernel: 6.1.0-134-generic (x86_64)
Consult /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/560.45/build/make.log for more information.
make[1]: *** [kernel] Error 2
```

maya: make.log shows unresolved symbol: `nvidia_p2p_get_pages` during module link. Also /dev/nvhost never appears. Node ends up in failed state and doesn't join GKE nodepool.

oncall-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-560-dkms-eu-west2 (severity: medium). Notifying oncall.

dmitri: Can you paste the tail of the make.log and dmesg? Also which CUDA runtime/container image is the canary using?

maya: Tail from make.log:
```
...
Undefined symbols:
  nvidia_p2p_get_pages
  nvidia_p2p_put_pages
ld: error: symbol referencing errors
```
And dmesg shows: 
```
[   11.234567] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
[   11.234580] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
[   11.345678] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: failed to reserve memory: -12
[   11.345690] nvhost: probe of 0000:01:00.0 failed with error -22
```

raj: That memory error (-12) is ENOMEM? Could be firmware/PCI BAR layout differences on newer kernels. Did we run the same kernel build flags in our provis images?

leah: We recently bumped the host kernel config for preemption and changed CONFIG_IOMMU_STRICT in the ubuntu-6.1 image for perf testing. If DKMS modules are built against slightly different headers or KBUILD_* flags that could change symbol expectations.

dmitri: Two immediate checks: 1) confirm kernel-headers package version on failing nodes equals /lib/modules/6.1.0-134-generic; 2) reproduce module build manually in a canary container with the same headers. If the headers don't match, DKMS won't link properly.

maya: Verified headers match (sha256 same). Reproduced build in chroot: the link still fails. Suspect the ABI change came from upstream NV driver expecting a newer kernel API (or missing compat shim).

raj: Could we force the driver to build with "--compat-module-version" or apply a small patch to provide the missing symbols as weak links? Risky for production.

leah: Before patching, try booting a canary with the older 555-series driver binary blob (pre-built) to see if the nodes provision normally. If they do, we can pause 560 rollout and debug more.

maya: Did that. Nodes with prebuilt 555 blob came online fine and joined the pool. So 560 build-time failure is the blocker.

ops-bot: Note: rolling back canary to 555-series will free up 8 GPUs in eu-west2, ETA for re-provision ~18m.

dmitri: Also check NCCL and CUDA compatibility matrix — some new driver symbols are used by cuDNN/CUDA runtime 12.x. If our default runtime image uses CUDA 12.2 it's possible the driver source expects those symbols.

maya: Canary images were using cuda:12.1-runtime. I'll try switching to a 12.2 container and rebuild DKMS inside it.

leah: Another angle: are these nodes on a mix of firmware versions? We had an OEM firmware roll earlier this month for some instance types. PCI BAR differences could explain failed memory reservation.

maya: Good call. I checked instance metadata: failing nodes are mostly c2-standard with firmware v1.9. Some healthy nodes were firmware v1.8. Opening a ticket with infra vendor.

dmitri: For short term: pause 560 rollout. Add a pre-provision hook that validates DKMS build in a chroot and verifies /dev/nvhost creation before promoting node to the pool. That avoids half-provisioned nodes.

maya: Implemented a pre-provision check script and paused canary. I'll push a patch to the provisioner repo and trigger a quick canary using the prebuilt 555 driver.

raj: Also create an eval job to compile 560 from source on kernel 6.1+ with debug symbols and get full linker map. Might reveal missing symbol origin.

leah: If vendor firmware is root cause, we need to coordinate firmware rollback or request a PCI firmware patch. Either way, keep the region capacity updated; ops-bot, please block automated scale-ups to eu-west2 until we confirm firmware status.

ops-bot: Auto-scaling to eu-west2 paused by automation (reason: suspected driver/firmware incompatibility).

maya: Thanks all. I'll attach logs to the incident and update once we have vendor reply or DKMS repro. For now, hold 560 and default back to 555 for eu-west2. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident updated: severity unchanged. Assigned to maya/dmitri.

leah: P.S. add a note to rollout runbook: "Always validate kernel config + firmware parity between canary and fleet before driver upgrades."

maya: Adding runbook note now."
